title: Vendor terms triage — personal scratchpad
content:
Quick objective: fast triage of incoming vendor MSA/SA/Order SOWs so we can: 1) identify true blockers (legal/regulatory/risk) 2) decide which items to escalate vs. trade, and 3) craft short negotiation scripts for AE/AM to use on first call.

Triage matrix (use this every time):
- Blocker (must resolve pre-sign): data residency/processing restrictions that conflict with customer setup, export controls, regulatory denial, unlimited liability or CPI exposure.
- High (likely pushback, escalate to legal lead): indemnity for third-party claims that includes Redwood IP, audit rights w/ production access, vendor subprocessing that isn’t disclosed.
- Medium (negotiate via playbook): SLA credits, termination-for-convenience notice length, transition assistance.
- Low (concessions acceptable): non-core warranty language, minor reporting obligations, branding/headline usage.

Clauses to scan first (quick checklist):
- Liability cap: default ask = greater of fees paid in last 12 months or $250k; prefer $500k for strategic infra vendors. If SaaS infra with data exposure, escalate.
- Indemnity: vendor must indemnify for IP infringement and third-party claims arising from vendor negligence; carve outs for combined products need careful review.
- Data use & ownership: vendor may only use customer data to provide services; no training of models on customer data unless explicit opt-in and anonymization.
- Confidentiality definition: confirm "Confidential Information" covers APIs, prompts, model outputs, and derived embeddings. Add duration (3-5 years post-termination) unless regulated.
- Security & SOC/pen tests: require SOC2 Type II or equivalent, breach notification within 72 hours, cooperation for investigation, encryption at rest and in transit.
- Subprocessors / subcontractors: notify and allow objection on reasonable grounds; list key subprocessors in schedule.
- Audit rights: limit to scope and frequency (no more than annually, written notice, redact PII); prefer third-party attestation in lieu of invasive audits.
- Export controls & sanctions: vendor must comply; vendor responsible for its non-compliance.
- Termination for convenience: 30–90 days notice; include transition assistance (30–90 days) and export of customer data in usable format.
- IP & residuals: vendor retains core model IP; protect customer-specific prompts/inputs/outputs; avoid broad residuals language that allows reuse of proprietary prompts.

Negotiation scripts (for AM/AE):
- If asked about model training on our data: "We treat customer data as confidential and only process it to provide the service — we don’t permit model training on customer data without explicit contractual opt-in. If training is required, we’ll discuss anonymization and compensation."
- If vendor asks for broad rights to use output: "We’re comfortable with you using anonymized aggregate metrics for service improvement, but not for training external models or for commercialization without a separate agreement."
- Liability cap pushback: "We’ll consider higher liability if you can provide SOC2+ attestations and cyber insurance limits that align with the increased cap."

Fallback language snippets I use often:
- Liability cap: "The aggregate liability of each party shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid by Customer to Vendor in the 12 months preceding the claim or (b) U.S. $250,000."
- Data training: "Vendor will not use Customer Data to train models for use outside the provision of Services without Customer’s prior written consent."
- Breach notice: "Vendor will notify Customer within 72 hours of becoming aware of a security incident affecting Customer Data and provide reasonable cooperation in remediation."

Decision heuristics for quick escalations (when to pull legal principal):
- Any clause that attempts to disclaim all liability for data exfiltration, or that pushes unlimited liability for customer losses.
- Any requirement for us to indemnify vendor customers or third parties beyond gross negligence/willful misconduct.
- Vendor wants access to raw PII and to retain it indefinitely.

Practical notes / reminders:
- Always check SOWs for conflicting term language (SOW > MSA? confirm priority).
- If vendor uses subcontractors in APAC/EU, check cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs or equivalent).
- Keep a one-liner summary at top of ticket for sales: "Key risks: DATA_TRAINING, LIABILITY_CAP, AUDIT_RIGHTS".

Next steps (for current deal CONTRACT-4521):
1) Mark liability cap as high-priority (vendor suggested unlimited cap).
2) Insert training prohibition language and ask for subprocessors list.
3) Ask AM to use the "training" script on next call and note vendor response in Jira.
4) If vendor refuses training restriction, escalate to me + head of product for risk acceptance.

Notes to self: keep templates updated in repo/contract-templates. If we accept higher liability cap, require cyber insurance proof and add SLA/uptime targets tied to credits. Put redline back to vendor with tracked changes and a 2-page summary for sales (one-pager wins).

Unresolved questions to log in ticket: what is acceptable cap for long-term infra partners (>=3 years)? add to Confluence decision tree.

End of scratchpad.

(Edited during 1:1 with Samir, 2026-03-10)
